blocks.hero.subhead: No guessing and no surprise bills. Here is every counselor's rate, how payment works, and how you may be able to get part of it back from your insurance.
blocks.request.heading: Ready to get started?
blocks.request.text: Request an appointment in about a minute, or call (502) 523-2970. Most people are seen the same week.
blocks.rates.heading: Rates by counselor
blocks.rates.note: Every session is 50 minutes. Each name links to that counselor's profile. The rate is the same in person or online.

more.body:
Sessions with Sophie Bowman, our Student Counselor, are $50. Sophie works with children 8 and up, teens, and young adults, and her work is supervised by Tony Gore, LCSW. [Meet Sophie](/sophie-bowman)

**If cost is a concern,** talk with us before you rule counseling out. We consider financial hardship case by case.
more.heading: Looking for a lower cost?

more.body:
We don't bill insurance directly. You pay for each session (HSA and FSA cards work), and we'll give you a superbill: a receipt with the details your insurance company needs. If your plan has out-of-network mental health benefits, you can submit it to be reimbursed for part of the cost.

**How to find out what you'd get back:** call the number on your insurance card and ask:

1. Do I have out-of-network benefits for outpatient mental health?
2. What's my deductible, and how much of it have I met?
3. What percentage do you reimburse for an out-of-network session?
4. How do I submit a superbill?
more.heading: Do you take insurance?

more.body:
We accept credit and debit cards, HSA and FSA cards, cash, and checks. Payment is taken after each session. You can keep a card on file to be charged automatically after each session, or pay at the front desk each time if you'd rather.

**Cancellations:** please give at least 24 hours' notice if you need to cancel or reschedule. A cancellation with less than 24 hours' notice is charged 50% of your session fee. A missed session without notice is charged the full session fee.
more.heading: How payment works

more.body: Under federal law, if you don't use insurance (or pay on your own), you have the right to receive a Good Faith Estimate of what your care will cost. You'll receive one before your first session, and you can ask for one anytime. [cms.gov/nosurprises](https://www.cms.gov/nosurprises)
